limitations: The sharp iff theorem concerns only the leading KLT mode versus DCT DC. The correction-factor result gives a non-uniformity lower bound and a necessary scale, not full-basis sufficiency. Fixed-mode limits do not control indices growing with N, and the Rayleigh-efficiency formula is not a total coding-gain theorem. Full texts of several older transform references were not inspected, leaving residual originality risk; the motivating preprint is recent.
provenance: Analytic joint-size/high-correlation consequences of the exact AR(1) KLT secular equations and the DCT-core factorization in arXiv:2609.20221, compared with classical KLT/DCT endpoint and performance-equivalence literature.
record_title: A 1/N boundary layer in the DCT endpoint of the AR(1) KLT
